claim_results.reason: Both metric formulas agree with independently computed high-precision projections: 72 cases, including extreme widths, large coefficients and a smallest-subnormal nonzero normal, had maximum normwise error 8.93e-17. Exact-zero normals return independent unchanged copies; invalid inputs and unrepresentable outputs are rejected. Executing the historical AST reproduces derivative -8.665090650287976 despite its zero average-based dot product. Direct integration independently confirms the supplied exact SL derivative -13.75720905043744. For n2R4SUP, executing the actual historical grid integration and projection gives first variation -1.2468250761882778, whereas the repaired direction gives -2.04e-15. Tangency verification genuinely integrates f*h separately from the projection dot product.

All 33 snapshot hashes and the candidate/dependency identities match. Execution used a fresh private copied tree without modifying the source project. Normal and -O author regressions passed all six groups, including 41 invalid-input cases each. All four required CLI cases reproduced their supplied numerical data and logs exactly; defaults, width-weighted execution and R=1 also worked. Independent adaptive integration verified weighted normalization and unweighted pairings, with errors below 1.4e-15 in the selected checks. Closed-form Fourier pairings and density-scaling identities verified second-variation signs, indexing and independence from the weighted-pairing argument. Zero/negative FD endpoint densities are rejected without clamping; a positive finite-step scaling example matches its exact answer. No required current runtime check remained unavailable.

Cutoff, quadrature and FD sensitivity data reproduced exactly. The small INF sample retains relative discrepancies 0.00500932 at 61 modes and 0.0000477975 at 241 modes; double-precision cancellation also reproduced. Reported counts, residuals and sampled signs match the data. P2b historically used integral-based projection and is correctly distinguished from the block-average defect. At the default P3 width, independent bump pairings reproduce Q within 2.6e-13, and spatial/shape checks confirm the negative half-acceleration factor. Current reports appropriately avoid universal sign, optimality or eta-limit conclusions. However, a positive but unresolved bump-width control silently eliminates every bump and produces misleading zero contributions, as detailed in F1.

findings.problem: P3 does not reject bump supports that cannot be resolved in floating-point coordinates. Rounded breakpoints can collapse onto the interface; np.unique then removes the support intervals and the sampled direction becomes identically zero.
findings.reproduction: Running the copied CLI with arguments '2 4 sup --bump-width 1e-20' exits 0 both normally and under -O. At the first interface, left endpoint, center and right endpoint all equal 0.29343444668877966. All three reported Q_linear_fixed_bump values are 0.0. The first requested direction has mathematical integral -1.890425317273808, while the implemented sampled direction has integral zero. Partial resolution loss also occurs at half-width 1e-16: a single unit-mass bump integrates numerically to approximately 0.83852.
findings.requested_change: Reject widths whose supports or quadrature nodes cannot be resolved, or evaluate the bump integrals in suitable local coordinates. Add normal and -O regressions for collapsed supports and partially resolved supports. The default-width results need not be discarded.

limitations: Numerical checks provide no rigorous spectral-tail bound, certified root enumeration, interval quadrature certificate or exact stationary-point certificate.
Finite sampled signs and P3 comparisons establish neither universal definiteness, box-constrained optimality nor an eta-limit Hessian identity.
Extended-precision projection checks used the supplied environment's longdouble implementation; other platforms were not tested.

Some artifacts referenced by author manifests, including run_evidence.py and source_preservation.json, were not supplied. Their historical execution and worktree-preservation assertions were not independently verified.
Unrelated analytic claims, unused dependency branches and complete formalization were outside this review.
